label: Chapter 2: The shapeshifter at the castle

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Tall? Another giant?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A different one. Lange Wapper.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Another legend, from Antwerp's folklore.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Give me the short version.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: He's a shapeshifter. In the version I found, he starts as a baby, raised by an Antwerp family, and grows into a giant who can change size and shape.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Is he nice?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Mixed. He helps people at first.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Later he's a trickster. He frightens drunks at night, and plays tricks on children.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So, a night-time prankster.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And a nuisance. One detail people like: he disliked the Virgin Mary.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: So the story goes that residents put little statues of her on their houses to keep him away.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Wait. That's why there are Madonnas on the corners of the buildings?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Not quite. Antwerp does have many street-corner Madonnas, but I can't tell you from my sources that Wapper is the reason.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That's the story. Treat it as a story.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Fair. And how does it end?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Two endings. He leaves the city for good.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Or he drowns in the Scheldt.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Two endings is cheating.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's folklore. It does that.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Where do I find him?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: By the river, in front of Het Steen, the old fortress.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: There's a bronze statue of him by the sculptor Albert Poels, from 1963.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: You can't miss it. He's a giant.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: I'll keep my eyes up.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And Het Steen is next, because it has its own dark side.
